questions.question: If you find something unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Drive the trip anyway and fix it later at a mechanic.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Avoid using the unsafe parts but continue driving.

questions.explanation: You must fix any unsafe issue found during a pre-trip inspection before driving. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: Where water pools on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water pools on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tires make it more likely. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What is true about a fatigued driver?

options.text: They should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
They may react slowly to dangers.
They are usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may react slowly to dangers.
questions.explanation: A tired driver will not see or react to hazards as quickly as an awake driver. Fatigue makes it harder to make quick, critical decisions.

questions.question: How should the exhaust system be during a vehicle inspection?
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must have no loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: What is true when approaching an active railroad crossing?

options.text: You will hear any approaching train.
You may not hear a train as it approaches.
You will hear two short horn blasts from the train.
There will always be flashing warning lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train as it approaches.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you will hear a train. Some areas ban horn sounds, or your vehicle's noise may block it. Do not rely on warning lights or signals to alert you.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be kept when a driver is away from the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to find. Leave them on the driver's seat when the driver is not in the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if brakes get too hot?

options.text: The air compressor cools them down.

questions.explanation: Overheated brakes can stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires near the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires near the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the control unit and wheel speed sensor wires near the brakes.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table show?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: How much water on a road surface causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to occur.

questions.question: What is a header board used for?

options.text: Help a driver see behind them.
Protect the driver from moving cargo.
Keep the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect drivers from cargo that may shift during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: Brakes heat up when used. If they get too hot, the heat causes expansion and chemical changes that make them less effective. Eventually they may stop working completely. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle and the engine is close to idle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine speed drops close to idle.

questions.question: How can you increase visibility at dawn or dusk when other vehicles have trouble seeing you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be prepared?

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transport.
questions.explanation: Brace containers so they cannot fall, slide, or bounce around during transport. All hazardous materials packages must be properly secured.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release it. If the pedal does not return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release it. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when the brake pedal is pressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times, then press it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in a brake system hold enough air so the brakes can be used several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When you stop on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by acceleration?

options.text: Remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids often happen on slippery roads. You can usually stop this type of skid by removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.question: On a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads. It is harder to stop and turn on slippery surfaces, so adjust your speed to drive safely.
